note: worldserver.json - the game program's settings in this flavor (docs/decisions/0016-a-server-is-a-flavor.md). Reference: src/server/apps/worldserver/worldserver.conf.dist, whose setting names these are; the format is this project's (docs/decisions/0005-json-configuration.md). This file is part of the flavor and is shared with it, so it holds nothing one machine alone knows: the database logins, the world's id, the addresses and ports the program binds, the control endpoint and the paths of the machine's own files are in config/machine.json, section worldserver, and a key stated there wins over this file. A path that names this flavor's own content is relative to this folder. Only the settings the ported stages read are here - a setting arrives with the stage that reads it, so a key in this file is one the program actually uses.

Enable.doc: Enable the embedded world console when standard input is an interactive terminal.

QueueCapacity.doc: Maximum number of console requests waiting for the world update; must be positive.

StatusInterval.doc: How often the program says what it is doing: up time, accepted connections, the maps it hosts and the instances it holds open. The auth program's timer reads the same key.

MinWorldUpdateTime.doc: How long may pass before the world's loop does not bother to update, in milliseconds. The reference's own key of the same name (worldserver.conf, 1 ms): WorldUpdateLoop sleeps the remainder rather than updating twice inside it (Main.cpp:586-616). The loop is what calls the world's update, which tells the scripts every tick and sweeps the instance table on its own World.SweepIntervalMs.

Threads.doc: Network threads serving accepted connections; a connection goes to the thread with the fewest already.

Trace.doc: Every byte of every gameplay connection, in and out, at debug. It needs its logger: Logger.network.trace = 6,Console Server.

WorldPack.doc: The world pack whose maps, entry points and doorways this world serves - the folder that holds maps/, relative to this flavor's folder. What a world is is a file (docs/decisions/0014-the-world-content-is-a-pack.md); a record whose folder is not its map id, or a pack with no maps folder, stops the program rather than serving half a world.

InventoryFile.doc: The bags and items a character-creation screen is given - a record list, read at start-up, relative to this flavor's folder. A client with no items has no inventory model to draw.

EquipmentFile.doc: What a new character wears per campaign and profession - a record list of sets, read at start-up.

EquippedSlotsFile.doc: Which slot of the client's equipped bag each kind of item is worn in - a record list, read at start-up. The number is the client's own: a kind no row names is not worn, and a piece whose slot is wrong is a piece the character is drawn without.

CommandsFile.doc: The chat command surface: the names a player may type, what each takes, and which server operation it runs. A record list, read at start-up; a name it grants with no operation behind it is refused then, not when a player types it (docs/decisions/0011-the-command-surface-is-content.md).

DistrictAllotment.doc: How many players one district of an outpost holds before the next district is shown (R5). The allotment is tied to a machine's own efficiency, so it is the operator's number; the game's value is 100.

PartySizeCap.doc: The party cap this world applies when a map does not state its own (R15). 8 is the common cap in the game; some modes allow 12 and some instances 25, and a map row overrides this.

SpawnScatter.doc: How far around a spawn point a character is placed when it enters a map (R13), in the game's own units: every entry picks a random point of that map's list and lands within this radius of it.

InstanceTick.doc: Whether an instance keeps a clock at all (R33). The game ticks one; an operator may choose not to, and nothing that does not tick can be simulated.

SimulationTickMs.doc: How often a map's simulation is ticked (R33), in milliseconds. 100 is the working implementation's own number (ASURA/config/Server/intervals.json, tick_interval_ms: a 0x001E every ~100 ms, median 81, measured from the live client), and its clock wakes on that interval whatever the client is doing (ASURA/crates/asura-world/src/instance.rs:394-403); an operator may run faster or slower.

PingValue.doc: The number a ping reply carries (0x000D). 20 is what a working server sent and what the reference's own log carried (0D 00 14 00 00 00); the client echoes it back in its own ping.

SweepIntervalMs.doc: How often the world checks its instance table for copies to dispose (R33, R40), in milliseconds. The reference's own check is not measured; a second is what a fifteen-minute hold needs.

CompassRange.doc: The range at which an enemy is simulated (R34), in the game's own units. Outside it, enemies are not ticked - most enemies only exist while inside it.

ExplorableDisconnectHold.doc: How long an explorable instance is held for a reconnecting party after a network disconnect (R37), in seconds; 900 is 15 minutes. A party that leaves by any normal means disposes the instance at once, whatever this says (R40).

MissionButton.doc: Whether an outpost that offers a mission presents the 'Enter Mission' button (R56).

AgentHealth.doc: The health a player agent is created with, sent as agent int-property 42 at load. The game's value for a fresh body is 400.

AgentEnergy.doc: The energy a player agent is created with, sent as agent int-property 41 at load. The game's value for a fresh body is 25.

AgentEnergyRegen.doc: The energy regeneration a player agent is created with, sent as agent float-property 43. Zero is what the reference's own capture shows for a fresh agent.

AgentSpeed.doc: How fast a player agent walks, in units a second: the create message carries it and the client walks the model at it.

StartingOutpost.doc: The outpost a fresh character is placed in and has unlocked (R12, R14) - the one unlock a character starts with, and the map its own row names as its start. The login's placement names the same fact for a character with no map anywhere (authserver.json, FallbackOutpost); a different number here would hand a new character an unlock the login never sends it to.

PointBoxHalfExtent.doc: Half the side, in map units, of the box around a point-shaped doorway - the older shape that states one coordinate pair and no wall. A step crosses such a doorway only by intersecting a box edge; a doorway stated as a wall does not use this at all, and 0 disables point doorways (ASURA/config/Server/portals.json, point_box_half_extent; ASURA/crates/asura-world/src/portals.rs:31-64).

TravelExplorable.doc: What the redirect's is_explorable field (0x01A6) carries: 0 for every travel (the default), 1 for every travel, or auto for the destination's own kind - which is what a live server sends. The default is 0 because that is the value an explorable's load against this server completes at: at 1 it waited 5138 ms from the redirect to the players block against 849 ms at 0 over the same walk (ASURA/crates/asura-world/src/travel.rs:21-42).

MaxAllowedCorrection.doc: How far, in game units, a client may place itself when it cancels a walk (0x8047) and still be believed. A correction farther than this from where the server thought the agent stood is ignored: the agent stops where the server believes it is and nothing goes on the wire, so the client is never ordered backwards. The reference's MAXIMUM_ALLOWED_CORRECTION (GmAgent.c:547-563); the working implementation runs it at 250 (ASURA/config/Server/movement.json).

Appearance.doc: The packed appearance word a character with no bits of its own is drawn with - 51380224 is 0x03100000, profession 1 (Warrior) with hair style 3, everything else zero. An all-zero word is Profession_None, which the client cannot build a model from.

EffectiveConfig.doc: Every setting this program read from this file, with any database password masked, at debug. It needs its logger: Logger.server.loading = 6,Console Server.

WorkerThreads.doc: Asynchronous connections to the login database.
Asynchronous connections to the world database.

SynchThreads.doc: Synchronous connections, used where the caller cannot wait.

WorkerThreads.doc: Asynchronous connections to the character database.

Trace.doc: Every statement both pools run, as a debug line. It needs its logger: Logger.sql.trace = 6,Console Server.

Console.doc: Type, level, flags, then the type's own fields. Type 1 is the console and its last field is the colour list for fatal, error, warn, info, debug, trace.

Server.doc: Type 2 is a file: the name, then the mode (a append, w overwrite).

Errors.doc: Errors on their own file, so a service manager can watch one of them.

root.doc: Level, then appender names. A logger inherits from its dotted parent and finally from root.

sql.sql.doc: Database failures, on the error appender.

time.update.doc: The clock the world advances by.
